## Changes since 9.3.0-dzbarsky28

Backports [PR #36](https://github.com/dzbarsky/bazel/pull/36), authored by Michael Mitchell.

### Configured query results as build inputs

The native `gencquery` rule evaluates a configured query over the transitive closure of its declared `scope` targets and exposes the result as an ordinary build output. Unlike `genquery`, it reflects the dependencies selected by the current configuration. Consumers do not execute the scope targets' actions merely by consuming the query result.

Supported output formats are `label`, `label_kind`, and `starlark`. Starlark formatting accepts either a `starlark_expr` or a `starlark_file` source label. Scope and formatter changes invalidate the result; output is ordered by label and configuration. `compressed_output` writes GZIP output.

The rule requires `--track_incremental_state`. Target patterns must name individual targets; wildcard/recursive patterns and generated formatter files are unsupported. Formatter files cannot use `load()`. Existing `genquery` and command-line `cquery` behavior is preserved.

The backport adapts option fields and structural ordering to Bazel 9.3. It does not add the newer `config(..., anyexec)` command-line syntax.

### Validation

Passed `GenCqueryIntegrationTest`, `GenQueryIntegrationTest`, `genquery_tests`, `ConfiguredTargetQuerySemanticsTest`, and all five shards of `configured_query_test` on the backport. All 21 immutable-release publication checks passed.

### Release publication

Linux and macOS binaries for x86_64 and arm64 are built and version-checked before publication. The immutable release includes SHA-256 checksums and build-provenance attestations.
